Trust decision: outbound HTTP may or may not reach a denied host is decided only by a case-sensitive `denylist.IsHostBlocked` URL check at write time / per request, with most clients on `http.DefaultClient`/`&http.Client{}`; the fix moves it to TCP-dial time via `denylist.NewHTTPTransport` behind one shared client.
`pattern_fit`: A+B — the fix spans executions, actions-v1, IDPs, SAML metadata and notification webhooks, plus two untouched routes (org-domain verification `http.Get`, SMTP XOAuth2 token endpoint).
Strongest lever: the notification webhook/SET channels are a real second HTTP implementation, and the pinned defaults document the denylist only for "execution target's endpoints" — an easy "never covered" dismissal.
Biggest red flag: none of the listed flags apply; the practical concern is size — the published fix touches 56 source files (≈120 min), far beyond a 45-minute fair solve, so the hidden tests must target a narrow subset.
